# XOR Cancellation — Identical Bits Remove Each Other

## The identity to remember

$$
x\oplus x=0,\qquad x\oplus0=x
$$

**Every symbol explained:** x is an integer represented in binary; ⊕ is bitwise exclusive OR; 0 is the all-zero bit pattern.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For x=6 (binary 110), 110 XOR 110 = 000 = 0. Also 110 XOR 000=110.

## Why it is true

At each bit, XOR returns 1 exactly when the inputs differ. Matching bits therefore cancel; associativity and commutativity let repeated values pair off regardless of order.

## Algorithm or number puzzle application

In an array where every integer appears twice except one, XOR all values to recover the single value.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

For [4,1,4,7,1], (4⊕4)⊕(1⊕1)⊕7=7. The cancellation is algebraic and O(1) extra space.

## Your turn

It only solves this exact multiplicity structure; if an item appears three times or several distinct singles remain, a simple XOR may not recover what you want.

**Memory rule:** Remember the mathematical structure behind the bit or counting operation, not a memorised code template.
